verdict.rationale: Codex documents all three distribution paths. Teams can check skills into the repo, which Codex discovers by scanning `.agents/skills` up to the repo root. Repo and local marketplaces are named team-distribution sources, added via `codex plugin marketplace add`, and skills can be packaged as installable plugins. A hands-on probe confirmed a skill installed into `./.agents/skills` from the catalog. Missing for 10: no evidence of admin-enforced org-wide rollout, and docs note marketplace availability can vary by surface.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can distribute a standard skill set to my whole team — via a marketplace, a shared repo, or files committed to the project

citations.quote: teams can check in skills relevant to a working folder. For example, skills only relevant to a microservice or a module.
Codex scans `.agents/skills` in every directory from your current working directory up to the repository root.
Local and repo marketplaces are separate authoring, testing, and team-distribution sources, and their availability can vary by surface.
Use `codex plugin marketplace add` to add and track a marketplace source instead of editing `config.toml` by hand.
Use skills to design the workflow itself, then package it as a plugin when you want other people to install it.
